results.title: Intergenerational mobility and emigration willingness and ...
results.content: As for individual-level controls, we account for variables that have been identified in the relevant literature as important covariates of emigration willingness and intentions: age and age-squared – individuals’ age has been shown to affect emigration intention non-linearly (Ivlevs and King Citation2015); marital status – studies generally show that marital status, particularly being married, might affect emigration willingness and intentions (Van Dalen, Groenewold, and Schoorl Citation2005); the number of children – paternalistic preferences may positively or negatively affect decisions related to emigration, while larger households may maintain stronger networks, which could promote individuals’ emigration willingness and intentions (Leeves Citation2009); the use of a mother tongue that is different from the main language of the country – this variable is a proxy for ethnic links with the country of residence (Ivlevs Citation2013); rural residence, subjective socio-economic rung, labor market status at the time of interview – all these variables reflect the structural positioning of individuals in the socioeconomic hierarchy and are shown to be associated with emigration willingness and intentions (Ortensi and Barbiano di Belgiojoso Citation2018; Van Dalen, Groenewold, and Fokkema Citation2005); life satisfaction – it has been suggested that a country’s political and economic conditions might affect emigration intentions indirectly through life satisfaction (Otrachshenko and Popova Citation2014). For accurately interpreting the substantive significance of interaction effects (Brambor, Roberts Clark, and Golder Citation2006), in , we present the marginal effects of subjective perception of intergenerational downward mobility on willingness and intentions to emigrate mediated by the level of economic development in countries where individuals were interviewed.
